title: Destination Cache
question_description:
Amazon’s fulfillment centers process millions of package routing requests daily. To optimize the sorting system, the most frequently accessed package destinations are temporarily stored in memory. However, server memory is limited. Design and implement a data structure for a Least Recently Used (LRU) Cache to manage these package routes. It should support the following operations in O(1) average time complexity:
- get(key): Retrieve the value of the key if it exists in the cache.
- put(key, value): Insert or update the value of the key. If the cache reaches its capacity, it should invalidate the least recently used item.

title: Gold Thief
question_description:
There are n houses built in a street, each of which contains some gold bars in it: gold[i]. A thief is going to steal the maximal bars for houses, but he can’t steal in two adjacent houses because if he does it will make create suspicion and he will be caught.
How many gold bars can you steal at most?
Follow-up:
- what if we must skip 2 houses?
- what if it's circular such that first and last house are considered to be adjacent?

title: Block Words
question_description:
You have a collection of baby blocks (cubes with single upper-case letters of the alphabet on each side).
Each block could have up to six different letters on it (or even more if we're in a universe with more than 3 dimensions), but for the sake of simplicity, we'll assume for now that each block only has two distinct letters.
The problem is to write a function that takes a collection of blocks and a target word and returns true or false depending on whether or not you can spell the target word with the collection of blocks.
Example:
(B,A),(A,B),(X,Y),(A,B): "BABY" => true
(B,A),(A,B),(L,E),(A,B): "ABLE" => false (since L and E are on the same block)

title: Character Separation
question_description:

If no such rearrangement is possible, throw an exception.

Conversion Rate

Rates: ['USD', 'JPY', 110] ['US', 'AUD', 1.45] ['JPY', 'GBP', 0.0070]
To/From currency ['GBP', 'AUD']

Given an array of delivery times, output the median of all values seen so far after each new delivery time arrives.

Input: [5, 17, 100, 11]

question_description: We need a library for finding files that match a condition. For now we have only two conditions ­ "the filename contains " and "the file extension is ". In the future we will want to support more. Conditions can be combined in a query. For example, "filename contains foo && (extension = png || extension = jpg)".

title: Raffle Winners
question_description: An e-conmerce platform wants to implement a promotional raffle system for a major sales event. Customers earn raffle entries based on their total spending during the promotional period. The probability of winning should be proportional to spending: a customer who spent $50 should have 5x the chance of winning compared to someone who spent $10. Write a function that takes a list of transactions (customer_id, amount) and returns K unique winners.

question_description:
You are given a log of website visits. Each log entry contains:
- Time – when the page was visited
- Customer ID – the user who visited the page
- Page – the page that was visited
Your task is to determine the most frequently visited sequence of three consecutive pages (a 3-page sequence) across all customers.
Example

T0     C2         E
T1     C1         B
T1     C2         B
T2     C1         C
T2     C2         C

T4     C1         E

- C2: E → B → C → D → A

title: Tree Kyoukai
question_description:
Given a root of a Binary Tree, return its boundary traversal in the following order:
- Left Boundary: Nodes from the root to the leftmost non-leaf node, preferring the left child over the right and excluding leaves.
- Leaf Nodes: All leaf nodes from left to right, covering every leaf in the tree.
- Reverse Right Boundary: Nodes from the root to the rightmost non-leaf node, preferring the right child over the left, excluding leaves, and added in reverse order.
Note: The root is included once, leaves are added separately to avoid repetition, and the right boundary follows traversal preference not the path from the rightmost leaf.

Amazon has to process numerous critical business intelligence jobs a day. Most of those tend to be very computationally heavy in nature such that they require a single virtual machine while they run and need to be guaranteed to run between certain times.
Given a set of jobs we need to know how many virtual machines we will need to provision? That is, given a set of jobs with start and end times like {(6,8), (2,5), (3,7)}, calculate the number of virtual machines required to execute all those jobs?

title: Distributed Sort-Softmax
question_description:
You are given an extremely large array of floating-point numbers that cannot fit into the memory of a single GPU. You have access to 4 GPUs connected via a high-speed interconnect (e.g., NVLink), and you may use collective communication primitives (e.g., all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, broadcast).
Your task is to:
- Sort the array globally across all 4 GPUs using collective operations.
- Compute the softmax of the entire array:
[
   \text{softmax}(x_i) = \frac{e^{x_i}}{\sum_j e^{x_j}}
   ]
- Optimize the pipeline to compute the final softmax output in a single pass over the data, minimizing memory movement and synchronization overhead.
Assumptions
- Each GPU initially holds a disjoint partition of the array.
- Communication between GPUs is expensive relative to local computation.
- You may assume access to standard collective primitives:
AllReduce
AllGather
ReduceScatter
Broadcast
- AllReduce
- AllGather
- ReduceScatter
- Broadcast
Part 1: Distributed Sorting
Design an algorithm to sort the full array across all GPUs.
Questions to consider:
- How will you partition data across GPUs?
- Which collectives will you use to ensure global ordering?
- How do you minimize communication overhead?
Part 2: Distributed Softmax
After sorting, compute the softmax across the entire array.
Questions to consider:
- How do you compute the global denominator efficiently?
- How do you ensure numerical stability?
- Which collective(s) are required?
Part 3: Single-Pass Optimization
The naïve approach requires multiple passes:
- One pass to compute the max (for stability)
- One pass to compute the sum of exponentials
- One pass to normalize
Challenge: Design a method to compute softmax in a single pass over the distributed data.
Questions to consider:
- Can you fuse reductions?
- How can you combine max and sum computations?
- What trade-offs exist between memory, latency, and numerical precision?
Follow-ups
- How would your solution scale to N GPUs?
- How would your design change if GPUs were connected over slower networks (e.g., Ethernet)?
- Can you overlap communication and computation?
- What are the failure modes (e.g., overflow, underflow, skewed data)?

title: Friendship Path
question_description:
Consider a popular social networking website, Facebook for example.
People can create their own profile and add the profiles of others to their friends list.
You are given two Facebook profiles, "Gordon" and "Stephen".
I would like to find out how to get from Gordon's profile to Stephen's profile by navigating through Gordon's friends,
then friends of friends and so on. For example:
    * Gordon
    * Shantel (who is friends with Gordon)
    * Maria (who is friends with Shantel)

title: Friends Purchases
question_description:
Amazon is releasing a new feature called "Stuff Your Friends Are Buying." This feature aims to list a set of products that you have not already purchased, chosen from the items your friends have bought. The list should be ordered from most bought to least bought.
To facilitate this, we have access to the following two APIs:
- getPurchases(person): Returns a list of purchases made by the given person. If a product was purchased multiple times, it will appear multiple times in this list.
- getFriends(person): Returns a list of friends of the given person.
Task: Complete the function itemsFriendsPurchases(person) that takes a person (user ID) as input and returns a list of products that person's friends are buying, adhering to the following rules:
- Products must not have been already purchased by the input person.
- Products should be ordered from most frequently purchased by friends to least frequently purchased by friends.
- If no friends are found, or friends have no relevant purchases, return an empty list.

title: Fulfillment
question_description:
You are a software engineer at Amazon working on the Fulfillment Network routing system. The network consists of several fulfillment centers (represented as nodes) connected by bidirectional delivery routes.
A specific fulfillment center (the destination) is currently experiencing a shortage of a popular item and needs to request inventory transfers from nearby centers. However, due to delivery time constraints, the inventory can only be transferred if the sending center is within a certain number of delivery routes (maxStep) from the destination.
You are given the following inputs:
- connections: A 2D array of integers representing the bidirectional delivery routes between fulfillment centers (e.g., [u, v] means there is a direct route between center u and center v).
- destination: An integer representing the ID of the fulfillment center that needs the inventory.
- maxStep: An integer representing the maximum number of routes (edges) an inventory transfer can take to reach the destination.
- inventory: A hash map (or dictionary) where the key is the fulfillment center ID and the value is the current quantity of the item in stock at that center.
Task:
Write a function that returns an array of all fulfillment center IDs that can successfully transfer inventory to the destination center.
To be included in the result, a fulfillment center must meet all of the following criteria:
- It is not the destination center itself.
- It has at least 1 item in stock (inventory > 0).
- The shortest path from the center to the destination is less than or equal to maxStep.
The returned array can be in any order.

title: Package Installation
question_description:
We are in charge of designing a system to install packages. We are required to support the installation of a package and all of its dependent packages. Define what a package looks like and code a solution to this problem.
Clarification with the interviewer:

- We can indicate a package with string, the dependency package with string as well.
- Find All packages to install, and build up the relationship between them.
- We can define some existing functions to return all dependent packages to install for a certain package.
- Get the adjacency list to indicate the relationship between packages.
- This is a question about topological sort. The key is to detect the cycle dependencies.
- The input can be one package, or even a list of packages.

title: Playlist
question_description:
Imagine you are building a music streaming service. A core feature is the user's playlist. We need you to design and implement a Playlist class in the language of your choice.
Requirements: The Playlist class must support the following operations:
- add_song(song_name: str): Adds a new song to the very end of the playlist.
- remove_nth_from_end(n: int) -> str: Finds and removes the nth song from the end of the playlist. n=1 represents the last song, n=2 the second to last, and so on. This method should return the name of the song that was removed. If n is an invalid value (e.g., out of bounds), it should handle the error gracefully.
- print_playlist(): Displays the current playlist in order, from the first song added to the last. If the playlist is empty, it should indicate that.
Example Usage:
playlist = Playlist()
playlist.add_song("Bohemian Rhapsody")
playlist.add_song("Stairway to Heaven")
playlist.add_song("Hotel California")
playlist.add_song("Sweet Child O' Mine")

# Current playlist:
# 1. Bohemian Rhapsody
# 2. Stairway to Heaven
# 3. Hotel California
# 4. Sweet Child O' Mine

playlist.print_playlist()

removed = playlist.remove_nth_from_end(2) 
# Should remove "Hotel California"
print(f"\nRemoved: {removed}")

# Current playlist:
# 1. Bohemian Rhapsody
# 2. Stairway to Heaven
# 3. Sweet Child O' Mine

playlist.print_playlist()
Follow-up Question: After you've implemented the class, let's discuss how you would add a shuffle() method to the playlist. What would be an efficient algorithm to implement this?

title: Sawtooth Pattern String Builder
question_description:
You are given three inputs:
- An integer height representing the number of rows in a sawtooth pattern.
- An integer width representing the number of repeating zigzag segments.
- A string word consisting of uppercase English letters.
Write a function that arranges the characters of word into a sawtooth (zigzag) pattern with the given height and width, filling characters left to right across each segment. After constructing the pattern, return a string formed by reading the pattern row by row from top to bottom.
Pattern Rules
- Each segment forms a vertical zigzag:
Starts at the top row.
Moves diagonally down to the bottom row.
- Starts at the top row.
- Moves diagonally down to the bottom row.
- This zigzag repeats width times.
- Characters from word are placed sequentially into the pattern.
- If word has extra characters after filling full segments, continue the pattern as far as possible.
Example
Input:
height = 3
width = 2
word = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMN"

Pattern:
A B       F G       K L
    C   E       H   J       M
        D           I           N

Output:
"ABFGKLCEHJMDIN"

title: Word Trail
question_description:
You are given a continuous string of lowercase English characters without any spaces (e.g., "myhousehavecat").
You are also provided with a helper method, boolean isWord(String str), which queries a dictionary and returns true if the given string is a valid word, and false otherwise.
Task: Write a function that uses backtracking to segment the input string into a sequence of valid dictionary words. Return the result as an array of strings.
Notes / Constraints:
- There may be multiple valid ways to segment the input string. You only need to return one valid solution.
- You can safely assume that the input string will always have at least one valid segmentation.
- You cannot change the order of the characters in the input string.
Example:
input:
s = "myhousehavecat"
output:
["my", "house", "have", "cat"]
